title: No Sprinter Can Catch a Gibbon in the Treetops
subject: gibbon

scenes.text: Usain Bolt can't catch this animal. It never runs.
A gibbon swings through the treetops at up to thirty-five miles an hour.
Bolt's top speed was about twenty-eight.
One swing can carry it forty feet, with a drop of about two hundred feet below.
The secret is huge arms, hook-shaped hands, and shoulders that rotate far wider than ours.
So it moves arm over arm, faster than the fastest human sprinter, and it never touches the ground.

description:
Usain Bolt can't catch a gibbon, and the gibbon never even runs.
Gibbons swing through the treetops at up to 35 mph and leap about 40 feet, while Bolt topped out around 28 mph.
Could you keep up?
first_comment: Bolt hit about 27.8 mph. Gibbons beat that in the trees. Which animal should we race next?
